subject.title: ACP parent session stuck until refresh when yielded waiting for child completion

question: Should yielded-parent completion wakeups be owned by task terminal delivery, runtime-specific relays, or a new explicit yield-wait lifecycle state across ACP and native subagents?
rationale: Current main and the open PRs show multiple plausible partial seams; choosing the permanent cross-runtime ownership boundary is an architecture/product decision rather than a one-file repair.

options.title: Task/announce delivery owns wakeups
options.body: Use task terminal or announce delivery as the durable parent-continuation source for both ACP and native child completions, with runtime relays limited to progress.

options.title: Runtime relays own wakeups
options.body: Keep ACP/native-specific relays responsible for waking yielded parents, accepting separate code paths and regression coverage per runtime.

options.title: Add explicit yield-wait lifecycle
options.body: Introduce persisted yield-wait state and formal lifecycle events before landing further partial wake patches.

recommendation.title: Task/announce delivery owns wakeups
recommendation.body: Use task terminal or announce delivery as the durable parent-continuation source for both ACP and native child completions, with runtime relays limited to progress.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history shows the strongest direct work on subagent completion handoffs and active parent wake behavior.
